history.summary: The Jagannath Temple in Sector 4, Bhilai is a replica of the famous Jagannath Temple of Puri, Odisha, built in the Kalinga architectural style — the vimana (sanctum) in Rekha style and the jagamohana (porch) in Pidha style. It serves Bhilai's Odia community (many settled here with the Bhilai Steel Plant). The sanctum holds the wooden idols of Lords Jagannath and Balabhadra and Goddess Subhadra, approached by 22 steps as at Puri. The complex includes a Shiva shrine, a Garuda stambha, and shrines to Hanuman, Ganesh, Brahma, Vishnu, Maheshwara, Vimala, Lakshmi, Saraswati and the avatars of the Lord. Exact founding year and builder UNVERIFIED.

town_description: Bhilai is a major industrial city in Durg district, Chhattisgarh, best known for the Bhilai Steel Plant of SAIL, one of India's largest steel works. It forms a twin city with Durg, about 30 km west of Raipur. Planned industrial townships give it a mixed, pan-Indian population with many migrant communities.
